o1.biggest_strength: It targets the right problem: Essentials customers with 8+ channels, where churn and exit reasons clearly point to a flat agency-style plan with approvals.
o1.biggest_mistake: It underplays yearly billing even though yearly uptake is low and churn is much lower; I would want that included as part of the first rollout, not pushed to a later test.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a clear yearly-billing push in the recommendation, tighten the month-6 math, and make the test measure Team downgrade risk before a wider launch.

o2.biggest_strength: It finds the main leak, gives one clear recommendation, includes the churn and downgrade math, and remembers to use yearly billing as part of the switch moment.
o2.biggest_mistake: The revenue table is a little compressed and the base-case assumptions are doing a lot of work; I would want the math shown more plainly before sharing it with the board.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the revenue bridge easier to audit, use revenue-per-invited-customer as the main test metric, and soften the Team downgrade exposure with a tighter eligibility rule or clearer guardrail.

reason: Both are usable and pick the right pricing move, but Output 2 is closer to what I would hand to the team because it also tackles the under-used yearly option and faces the Team cannibalization risk directly. Output 1 has slightly better copy, but it leaves an important quick win on the table.
